heading: Order — Positive, Dialectical & Ultimate Terms
outline: Positive terms: hic et nunc, genus/differentiam, Bentham's real entities, Kantian manifold — the physicalist ideal (pp. 183–185)
Dialectical terms: Bentham's fictitious entities, polar vocabulary, phraseoplerosis/archetypation, action-and-idea order (pp. 184–187)
Church-spire example: nonverbal behavior as symbolic expression, dialectical realm permeating positive world (pp. 186–187)
Ultimate terms: parliamentary jangle vs. guiding-idea hierarchy, principle of principles, developmental sequence (pp. 187–189)
Platonic Republic Book VIII–IX: timocracy/oligarchy/democracy/tyranny as ultimate developmental series, four summarizing terms (pp. 188–189)
Ultimate elements in Marxist persuasion: class hierarchy as developmental series, concrete universal (Hegel), local participation in total dialectic (pp. 189–197)
Shylock/Ellison/Wright: transcendence-within-constraint, parliamentary jangle without ultimate resolution, vengeance as acceptance of opponent's rules (pp. 193–195)
Lenin's What Is to Be Done?: quid factum vs. quid faciendum, Proletarian as generic persona, rhetorical deliberative register (pp. 196–197)
Mannheim's sociology of knowledge: relativism vs. relationism, pro-ultimate status, limits of ideological unmasking (pp. 197–199)
Platonic dialogue reconstruction: five-step ascent from competing ideologies to mythic image; Mannheim's step-5 error (pp. 200–202)
Motivational problem: bias-as-promise; sociology cannot survive eliminating the mythic motive it would discount (pp. 201–202)
Mythic ground and context of situation: esthetic myth (Crane/Keats/Coleridge); Malinowski's context of situation; McKeon/Abelard contextual canons (pp. 203–207)
Contrast Mannheim vs. Platonic method; enargeia as rhetorical peak of the New Vision (p. 207)

concepts.label: Positive Terms
concepts.gloss: First vocabulary order: names grounded in perception, locatable in time and place, definable per genus et differentiam. The physicalist ideal reduces them to observable motion. Bentham's 'real entities'; Kantian sensory-intuition-plus-concept.

concepts.label: Dialectical Terms
concepts.gloss: Second vocabulary order: 'polar' terms (capitalism, Elizabethanism) whose meaning shifts by contrast. Belong to action/ideas rather than perception. Require paraphrase, behavioral testing, imaginal reading. Bentham's 'fictitious entities.'

concepts.label: Ultimate Terms / Ultimate Order
concepts.gloss: Third vocabulary order: a 'guiding idea' or 'principle of principles' that places competing dialectical voices in a developmental hierarchy rather than parliamentary jangle. Transcends and fulfills the dialectical order. Narrative's implicit equivalent is plot structure.

concepts.label: God-Term (apex of ultimate vocabulary)
concepts.gloss: The operative 'principle of principles' — the apex term that ranks all other motives in an ultimate vocabulary. Not named 'god-term' here but structurally present: in Platonic ultimate, the Form of the Good; in Marxist ultimate, the direction of historical necessity.

concepts.label: Hierarchy
concepts.gloss: The structural form of an ultimate vocabulary: a graded developmental series in which each stage both represents the universal principle of the whole and has its own moment of completeness. The formal difference between ultimate order and parliamentary compromise.

concepts.label: Identification (ultimate scope)
concepts.gloss: In this unit identification achieves its maximum vertical range: the local actor becomes consubstantial with the universal direction of a developmental series (the Marxist worker as 'the Proletarian' participating in total historical dialectic). Spine term developed at widest scope.

concepts.label: Consubstantiality (ultimate extension)
concepts.gloss: Consubstantiation extended from person/person or person/faction to actor/universal-principle: the worker shares substance not only with the class but with the developmental direction of history. Three levels: local act / class / universal direction.

concepts.label: Marxist Persuasion
concepts.gloss: Burke's primary case study in ultimate vocabulary. Rhetorical power derives from arranging classes in a developmental hierarchy grounded in the universe itself, enabling any local participation to be simultaneously particular and universal. Analyzed for its formal rhetorical structure, not its truth-claims.

concepts.label: Concrete Universal (Hegelian)
concepts.gloss: Any moment in a developmental series representing the universal essence of the series: the bud represents blossom, fruit, seed, decline, and futurity. Burke imports this to explain how an ultimate order can be simultaneously particular and universal.

concepts.label: Sociology of Knowledge (Mannheim)
concepts.gloss: Mannheim's 'relationist' project: systematic discounting of ideological bias by studying connections between ideologies and their nonverbal conditions. Burke classifies it as 'pro-ultimate' — more precise than relativism but unable to reach genuine ultimate order because it lacks a governing principle of principles.

concepts.label: Relativism vs. Relationism
concepts.gloss: Mannheim's distinction: relativism maps the diversity of ideological perspectives; relationism builds exact knowledge about connections between ideologies and their grounds. Burke treats relationism as a dialectical advance that still falls short of ultimate order.

concepts.label: Mythic Ground
concepts.gloss: Motivational level transcending discursive reason, figured in image rather than idea. In Platonic dialogue, the culminating mythic image figures a motive the dialectical ascent has prepared one to receive. Mannheim's error is treating mythic ground as equivalent to ideological bias.

concepts.label: Parliamentary Jangle / Horse-Trading
concepts.gloss: Burke's negative term for dialectical confrontation without ultimate resolution: compromise satisfying no one fully, each partisan forced into tactical concessions. Defines what ultimate vocabulary overcomes.

concepts.label: Context of Situation (Malinowski)
concepts.gloss: Positive-order analytic for verbal acts: the extraverbal customs, social psychology, and tribal organization implicit in any utterance. Generalizes the requirement that meaning cannot be separated from nonverbal scene. Applied also to Abelard's contextual canons in scholastic rhetoric.

concepts.label: Terministic Screen
concepts.gloss: Each vocabulary order constitutes a screen directing and deflecting attention: positive screen is physicalist/perceptual; dialectical screen is partisan/polar; ultimate screen ranks motives hierarchically. Switching screens changes what counts as a motive.

concepts.label: Unmasking / Ideology-Exposure
concepts.gloss: Mannheim's generalization of Marxist mystification-exposure: any doctrinal vocabulary carries partisan bias favoring some group's interests; opposing theorists can expose this partiality. Each unmasking is itself partial; cumulative process aims at ideological neutrality.

concepts.label: Enargeia
concepts.gloss: The vividness or visual immediacy of the 'New Vision' that transcends the imagery preparing it. Burke invokes it at the close of the unit as the rhetorical peak of an ultimate order — the experiential culmination toward which the developmental series aims.

concepts.label: Attitude (Incipient-Act Orientation)
concepts.gloss: Ultimate vocabulary organizes 'one's attitude toward the struggles of politics' (p.188) — an attitudinal realignment prior to any specific act. The worker who absorbs Marxist doctrine shifts from Mr. So-and-so to 'the Proletarian': a transformed incipient-act register.

concepts.label: Transcendence
concepts.gloss: The formal operation of each vocabulary order on the one below it: ideas transcend sensory percepts; mythic image transcends ideas. Also the social operation: an individual transcends inferior status by identifying with a higher-order motive. Man is a 'transcending animal' as symbol-user.

concepts.label: Phraseoplerosis and Archetypation (Bentham)
concepts.gloss: Bentham's methods for handling dialectical (fictitious-entity) terms: phraseoplerosis fills out the expression to make implicit modifiers explicit; archetypation discounts the misleading images contained in an expression. Burke adopts both as analytic tools for dialectical vocabulary.

positions.claim: Vocabulary has three irreducible orders — positive, dialectical, ultimate — each with distinct logical form and ontological reference; conflating them produces terministic impropriety.

An 'ultimate' vocabulary transforms parliamentary jangle into a developmental hierarchy by supplying a 'principle of principles' — a god-term — that ranks all competing dialectical voices in a single evaluative series.

The rhetorical strength of Marxism derives from its ultimate order: it allows local participation to be simultaneously particular and universal, enabling the worker to identify with the total dialectic of historical development.

Mannheim's sociology of knowledge is 'pro-ultimate' but cannot achieve a genuine ultimate order because its discounting method, if successful, would eliminate the mythic motive — the primary motive power — along with the ideological biases it targets.

The step from dialectical ideas to mythic image in the Platonic dialogue is simultaneously a step down (from purity of abstraction to impurity of image) and a step up (introducing a new motivational level beyond ideas). Treating this mythic step as equivalent to ideology is a categorical error.

Context of situation (Malinowski) demonstrates that verbal meaning is inseparable from nonverbal scene; even the most positivistic reduction of a ground contains a minimal 'mythic' element because verbal accounts are only 'suggestive' of what they describe.

calleja_pim_candidates.rationale: The god-term / ultimate win-condition orders all mechanical optimization (positive-term play): farming, rotating, trading efficiently are subordinate to the apex motive (rank, tier, narrative climax). Positive game-tokens (HP, gold) are the positive-vocabulary layer; their value is ranked by the ultimate term.

The ultimate-order framework maps onto a game's overarching story telos: the developmental sequence in which each story stage both represents the universal theme and prepares the next. The narrative god-term (destiny, chosen-one arc, ultimate redemption) is the apex that gives individual quest-acts their motivational weight.

Dialectical game-terms (skill, toxic, carry) are the polar vocabulary of the social dimension, acquiring meaning through contrast and community judgment. Parliamentary jangle without ultimate resolution = toxicity spirals, ELO anxiety, unresolvable disputes about play-style legitimacy.

The attitudinal transformation (Mr. So-and-so → 'the Proletarian') maps onto the affective shift when a player adopts a role-identity (support main, carry player) and begins experiencing game-events through that identity's motivational register rather than as neutral problem-solving.

The ultimate vocabulary's developmental series (each stage preparing the next, narrative necessity) maps onto the player's experience of game time as meaningful progression rather than merely sequential events. The Marxist logic of historical stages is structurally homologous to campaign/season arc temporality in games.

tensions.description: Ultimate order vs. parliamentary democracy: the hierarchical ranking of motives by a 'principle of principles' is formally superior to horse-trading but can be used unjustly — recognizing a 'low order of sociality' risks providing cover for morally unacceptable compromises.

Sociology of knowledge vs. mythic ground: Mannheim's discounting method, if fully successful, eliminates not only ideological bias but the mythic motivational energy that gives social life its primary zeal — the project is self-undermining at the limit.

Ultimate vocabulary and transcendence-within-constraint: for an oppressed minority, adopting an ultimate vocabulary (Marxism, nationalism) enables simultaneous particular and universal identification, but the tension between class loyalty and individual transcendence is never fully dissolved — it is managed by the ultimate order, not eliminated.

Image vs. idea at the apex: in ultimate rhetoric, should the culminating term be a pure idea (Socratic Form) or a mythic image? Burke shows that the esthetic myth (image transcending idea) and the discursive ultimate (idea governing images) are competing answers that generate different rhetorical effects.
